questions.q: In the local example, why is the label built only from orders after the cutoff?
options: Because pandas cannot use older orders
To make the dataset larger
So the features (past) and the label (future) do not overlap, avoiding leakage
Because AUC requires future data
questions.explain: Features use data before the prediction cutoff and the label uses data after it. Mixing them lets information about the outcome leak into the features.

questions.q: What does a point-in-time join guarantee?
options: Each event is matched with a feature value from after the event
Each event gets the latest feature snapshot at or before its own timestamp
All features are computed in one batch
Missing values are always zero
questions.explain: Point-in-time correctness reflects feature values as of the time each label was observed, never using later values.

questions.q: When translating a pandas group-by aggregation to PySpark, what stays the same?
options: The result is always a pandas DataFrame
Nothing; the logic must be redesigned
You must call .toPandas() first
The thinking: filter to the window, group by the entity key, aggregate
questions.explain: The logic is the same; Spark just distributes it and evaluates lazily. Avoid pulling huge tables into pandas.

questions.q: According to the Databricks docs, what can serve as a feature table in Unity Catalog?
options: Any Delta table with a primary key constraint
Only tables created through the Features UI
Any CSV file in DBFS
Only streaming tables
questions.explain: The docs state that any Delta table in Unity Catalog with a primary key can be a feature table.

questions.q: Why train with the DataFrame returned by training_set.load_df() and log with fe.log_model()?
options: It speeds up hyperparameter tuning
It converts the model to SQL
It removes the need for a registry
The model then looks up the same features at inference, reducing training/serving skew
questions.explain: A model logged with the feature client retains references to its features, so batch scoring and serving can look them up consistently.
